video_caption: The video opens with a close-up shot of a full moon, with a distinct, crescent-shaped shadow covering approximately the left third of its surface against a dark, starless sky. The moon itself is a pale gray, with visible craters and lunar maria. This view is maintained for several seconds before transitioning to a different scene at the 00:14 mark. The next shot shows a long, black telephoto camera lens, likely a Tokina AT-X AF SD 100-300mm f/4 lens based on visible branding, mounted on a black tripod. On top of the lens, a small green circuit board with various electronic components, identified as a Raspberry Pi camera module, is attached. A white ribbon cable extends from the module. Two thin blue wires run from the module down to a small, circular, black component attached to the side of the lens. The camera module has a small, darker black square, which is the camera lens, facing forward. The background is a plain, light gray surface. At 00:26, the scene changes again to an overhead shot of the Raspberry Pi camera module, now detached from the lens, lying on a light gray surface with its white ribbon cable unfurled next to it. To the left of the camera module is a black, circular object with a textured outer rim and a small, perfectly round hole in its center.

The video opens with a static shot showing a black, circular plastic object with an 8mm central hole lying on a light grey surface, next to a small green circuit board, which is a Raspberry Pi camera module, connected to a white ribbon cable. The camera module has a small black lens in the center. The scene then transitions to a close-up of the Raspberry Pi camera module resting on a piece of white foam. A pair of worn, dark pliers is firmly holding the camera module on the foam. A hand then enters the frame, holding a translucent white stick (identified by the audio as a cold hot glue stick). The hand uses this stick to press down on the camera lens on the circuit board and twist it counter-clockwise, effectively unscrewing the lens. The lens is successfully removed and placed on the foam next to the camera module. Finally, the camera module is shown from the underside, now attached to the black circular plastic object with four blobs of hot glue, while the white ribbon cable extends from it.

The video segment showcases the assembly and configuration of a custom camera setup. It begins with a close-up of a small, green circuit board covered in electronic components, connected by a white flat flexible cable (FFC) and secured with clear adhesive to a black, circular plastic lens cap. The scene then transitions to a large black camera lens, mounted on a tripod, with the circuit board attached to its rear. A green double-headed arrow highlights the distance between the rear of the lens and the circuit board, described as the "flange focal distance," crucial for focused images. Next, a black circular lens extension tube with "20mm" printed in white is presented. Finally, the video shows the completed setup: the large black lens mounted on a tripod, with the circuit board attached to its rear via the "20mm" extension tube. A small black circular sensor with blue wires is also affixed to the side of the lens, and a green arrow again indicates the length of the spacer at the back of the lens.

The video segment shows a long, black telephoto lens mounted horizontally on a dark grey tripod against a plain light grey background. A black lens hood is attached to the front of the lens. On the upper part of the lens barrel, a small green circuit board is mounted, featuring various electronic components and several wires. A white ribbon cable extends from the circuit board towards the right. Below the circuit board, a small, black circular component, possibly a sensor or motor, is attached to the lens barrel, connected to the circuit board by blue wires. Around 0:03-0:04, a person's hand with an index finger briefly enters the frame from the top left, points at the front of the lens hood, and then withdraws, leaving the lens stationary for the remainder of the clip.

The video opens with a close-up of a person's hands manipulating a black DSLR camera with a large telephoto lens attached. One hand presses a button on the camera body while the other hand rotates the lens, which has a textured grip and markings like "100". The person then detaches the lens from the camera body, revealing the metal mount and electronic contacts on the rear of the lens. A split screen appears, showing two views of the lens's rear: on the left, the aperture is wide open, displaying a large circular opening, while on the right, it is significantly closed, showing a small, constricted circular opening. The scene transitions to a top-down view of a small green circuit board, labeled "J2", "Raspberry Pi Camera Rev. 1.3", and with "P5V04A SUNNY" visible on a component, and "1368MLB 94V-0 MULTI 1 13 16" on another. A white ribbon cable extends from the right side of the board. A tiny black lens is placed above the circuit board. The camera zooms in on the central camera module, revealing a small, square lens and a colorful light sensor beneath it.

The video opens with a static, close-up shot of a green circuit board, featuring a black camera module at its center. The camera module has a small, square sensor visible inside, displaying green and purple hues. A gold flexible flat cable is connected to the left side of the camera module, bearing the text "P5V04A SUNNY". Various electronic components, including resistors and capacitors, are scattered across the circuit board. Text such as "D1", "R9", "J2", "1368MLB", "94V-0", "MULTI 1", "13:05", and "Raspberry Pi Camera" is visible on the board. The narration states that the zoom lens's focal length can reach up to 2700 millimeters. The scene then transitions to a static shot of a full moon against a pitch-black background, clearly displaying its craters and dark maria. The audio explains that this total view of the moon is obtained by adjusting the zoom to approximately 130 millimeters, which is equivalent to 1200 millimeters when used with the Raspberry camera module.

The video opens with a dark screen, then transitions to a clear, detailed shot of a full moon against a black background. The moon is grayish, with visible craters and dark areas (maria) across its surface, appearing relatively stable in the center of the frame. Around the 0:26 mark, a visual effect begins where a second, darker, crescent-shaped image of the moon appears from the left and overlays the full moon, progressively shadowing its left side. This transition creates the impression of a partial lunar eclipse. By the 0:32 mark, the moon is depicted as a partially eclipsed crescent, with the left portion significantly darkened, while the remaining illuminated part still shows its detailed, pockmarked surface against the dark expanse.

The video displays a close-up, static shot of the moon against a completely black background, indicating outer space. The moon is partially eclipsed, with a dark, curved shadow covering the upper left portion of its visible surface. The illuminated parts of the moon clearly show craters and variations in grey tones, highlighting its rugged texture. The image captures a moment during a lunar eclipse, with the shadow gradually progressing across the moon's face.

The video displays a close-up shot of a moon against a dark, black background, indicating it is night. The moon is mostly illuminated, but its left side appears slightly darker, suggesting a partial lunar eclipse or a shadow cast upon it. The surface of the moon is visible, showing craters and other topographical features, though they are somewhat blurry. At the 0:25 mark, there is a very brief and subtle visual effect where the moon appears to slightly shift or ghost, creating a fleeting double image, before immediately returning to its previous stable state for the remainder of the clip.

The video segment displays a time-lapse or sequence of a lunar eclipse, featuring the moon against a completely black background. From 00:01 to 00:38, a grey moon with visible craters and dark maria is shown, with a dark, curved shadow gradually covering its left side, indicating the progression of the eclipse. The moon remains relatively still in the frame during this period, but the shadow slowly advances. Around 00:38, there is a visual transition where the moon's image blurs slightly and then re-focuses, revealing a further progression of the eclipse. The shadow on the moon's left side has deepened and expanded, making the moon appear more like a crescent, with only a bright sliver of its surface visible on the right. The overall setting remains the vast, dark expanse of space.

The video segment displays a static, close-up shot of the moon against a completely black night sky. The moon is partially eclipsed, showing a prominent crescent shape with roughly half of its surface illuminated in a greyish-white hue, while the left half is in shadow. Visible details on the illuminated part of the moon include various craters and subtle textural variations on its surface. There are no people, objects, or text visible in the frame, and the visual remains constant without any changes or transitions throughout the entire segment.

The video displays a series of time-lapse shots focusing on a crescent moon against a pitch-black night sky, illustrating its progression through a lunar eclipse. Initially, from 0:00 to 0:19, a slightly blurred, wide crescent moon with visible craters is seen. A subtle transition or jump-cut occurs around 0:19, followed by the moon appearing to deepen into the Earth's shadow, becoming a narrower crescent between 0:24 and 0:34. Another subtle transition or cut is visible around 0:34, leading to a clearer view of the moon as a distinct crescent from 0:39 to 0:54, with the illuminated portion appearing to shrink further. Finally, from 0:58, the moon is shown as a very thin, sharp, and brightly lit crescent, marking the culmination of the observed eclipse phase. Throughout the video, the moon is the sole celestial body visible.

The video displays a time-lapse of the moon's surface against a pitch-black background. Initially, only a very thin, faint crescent of the moon is visible on the right side, with the rest shrouded in darkness (0:00-0:10). As the video progresses, the illuminated portion of the moon slowly expands from right to left, gradually revealing more of its surface details, including craters and darker regions (0:10-0:29). By the end of the segment, approximately half of the moon is brightly illuminated, forming a distinct half-moon shape, indicating a transition from a deep eclipse phase to a more illuminated state, as if emerging from Earth's shadow.

The video displays a close-up view of the moon against a black background, showing a partial lunar eclipse. The left half of the moon is brightly illuminated, revealing numerous craters and maria, while the right half is shrouded in the Earth's shadow, appearing significantly darker but still discernible. Throughout the video, the moon exhibits a slight shimmering or oscillating effect, particularly noticeable in the brighter areas, which is referred to in the accompanying audio as "scintillation." At approximately 0:25 and again at 1:08, there are brief visual transitions where a slightly shifted and similar image of the partially eclipsed moon momentarily overlays the current one before replacing it, suggesting a sequence of observations or adjustments. The moon maintains its partially eclipsed appearance for the duration of the video, with no further changes in its shadowed proportion.

The video segment commences with a close-up, steady shot of a gibbous moon against a black background, with the left side of its surface brightly illuminated and detailed, while the right side is shrouded in shadow. At approximately the 0:11 mark, a small, dark silhouette of an airplane, leaving a distinct reddish-brown contrail behind it, enters the frame from the bottom-left corner and begins to move diagonally upwards and across the illuminated portion of the moon's surface. The plane traverses the moon's face, with its contrail clearly visible stretching across the lunar features. The plane and its contrail eventually exit the frame towards the upper-right at around 0:42. For a brief moment, between 0:09 and 0:10, a faint, semi-transparent ghost image of the moon appears to overlap the main moon image, shifting slightly before the primary moon returns to its original clarity. The moon itself appears to drift slowly to the right and slightly downwards within the frame throughout the video, particularly after the airplane has passed.

The video opens with a static shot of the Moon, partially illuminated against a stark black background, showcasing its craters and dark maria. Over the first minute, the moon appears to slowly brighten, implying a progression through its phases, with the terminator (the line dividing the illuminated and dark portions) gradually receding. At 1:07, the scene transitions to a light gray background with black text, overlaid by a semi-transparent image of a full Moon. The text reads: "You can find more information about the stuff shown in this video and things concerning science and technology at the homepage of the project: www.HomoFaciens.de". This translates to "You can find more information about the stuff shown in this video and things concerning science and technology at the homepage of the project: www.HomoFaciens.de", indicating a call to action for viewers to visit a website for more details. At 1:15, the background remains light gray, and the text changes to: "Author: Norbert Heinz © You are allowed to copy and distribute this film for free This video was created with the help of open source software like: "Kdenlive", "Gimp", "Audacity" and more. Many thanks to the authors of the software." This text provides credit to the author, grants permission for free distribution, and acknowledges the open-source software used in the video's creation. An ambient, calm musical tone plays from 1:16 until the end of the video.
